title: Rigging in Houdini with APEX: 02 | Simple IK

steps.goal: Switch to create mode and drop down the skeleton joints
common_mistakes: Using Stash Input when you want to keep your work: it removes all existing changes and copies the input. Use Stash Merge Input to append instead. (official: SideFX Houdini docs: Skeleton (SOP))

Expecting Delete to remove a joint's children: it reparents them to the deleted joint's parent; Shift+Delete leaves them with their old parent chain broken. (official: SideFX Houdini docs: Skeleton (SOP))
assumptions: Before this: You are working at SOP level, in a geometry network, because the Skeleton node is a SOP.
steps.result: Joints are placed in the viewport.

steps.goal: Add an APEX AutoRig Component node for IK
common_mistakes: Writing #tag in the Multi IK Segments field: it expects the plain tag names. (official: SideFX Houdini docs: Rigging a character (KineFX / APEX AutoRig))
Enabling Enable Multithreading for one or two chains: it comes with an overhead and should only be used for many chains. (official: SideFX Houdini docs: IK Chains (SOP))
assumptions: Before this: A skeleton and the skin shape exist and are packed into one character with APEX Pack Character (defaults: Shape Path /Base.shp, Skeleton Path /Base.skel).
Before this: The skeleton points carry the tags the components look for (the docs add them with Attribute Adjust Tags); components select joints by tag.
Before this: A SOP skeleton on the first input and a second skeleton (or points) with the goal and optional twist points on the second input.
steps.result: An APEX AutoRig Component node is added and set to smooth IK.

how_to.text: Throw down an APEX AutoRig Component node and select Smooth IK from the component list.

check.text: Check that a APEX AutoRig Component now exists (Outliner or Node Editor).

steps.goal: Add a Marker node to expose joint names
common_mistakes: Using Plane on a perfectly straight chain: no plane can be computed, so the node shows a warning and falls back to Spine. (official: SideFX Houdini docs: Orient Joints 2.0 (SOP))
assumptions: Before this: A SOP skeleton is connected to the node's input.
steps.result: A Marker node is added with its text attribute set to name.

how_to.text: Add a Marker node and set the text attribute to name.
how_to.evidence: Instructor adds a marker node and specifies the name attribute.

check.text: Use the viewer state together with the parameter editor to see what each chain operation does to the joints' axes.
check.evidence: official: SideFX Houdini docs: Orient Joints 2.0 (SOP)

steps.visual_evidence: Marker parameter panel shows Text set to 'name'.
evidence: hit plus and put down a marker, and within here we want to have our text, right? So marker text and the attribute we want is the name attribute.

steps.goal: Add another APEX AutoRig Component node for FK
common_mistakes: Changing World Space after you already have edits on the pose: it will likely produce erratic results; use separate Rig Pose nodes for mixed local and world-space edits. (official: SideFX Houdini docs: Rig Pose (SOP))
Using Override and expecting input animation to survive: it replaces the input animation for that point. (official: SideFX Houdini docs: Rig Pose (SOP))
assumptions: Before this: A SOP skeleton or rig is connected to the node's input.
steps.result: An FK AutoRig Component is added before the IK component to initialize FK transforms.
